9232.name: Parts Pixie
9232.lore: Have you ever experienced this? Whenever you assemble a model, some parts always fall to the floor, never to be found again. That is because the Parts Pixies have hidden them away. These quantum lifeforms can only exist beyond one's field of vision and can never be truly observed. The Fools at the tavern claim the Red-Nosed Old-Timer loved models as a youth, and thus had many parts stolen. After stepping onto a mysterious Path, he captured a pixie with a story, making it willingly become one of his models. Afterward, he picked up the parts he had dropped in his childhood from the ground... and returned to his childhood.
9232.desc: When losing a Domain, obtain <unbreak>#1[i]</unbreak> random Blessing(s) of 1- to 2-star rarity. This Curio is destroyed after this effect triggers 5 times.

9233.name: A Ranger's Home
9233.lore: The Rangers of Deepspace Hunter made it a habit to save their last bullet for themselves, for their prey were the remnants of the Propagation and the Voracity, and the price of failure was far heavier than death itself. During the encirclement on Lidovia, the Rangers planned to trap a behemoth with ship anchors, then chisel away its flesh and destroy its organs like miners, killing it slowly. However, when their leader Triton's ship was swallowed whole by the beast, the fleet was forced to rout. Three days later, the behemoth suddenly dropped dead. The Rangers dug through the wreckage, only to find its viscera had been completely hollowed out, with Triton's corpse lying within the desiccated heart chamber. His last bullet still hung from his necklace, shining brightly.
9233.desc: The next time you select a non-Grand Miracle, it will definitely be an Extraordinary Miracle. This Curio is destroyed after the effect triggers

9234.name: You've Always Been Pretty
9234.lore: A Mirror Holder was attacked by pirates. Before dying, they entrusted the Mirror of Transcendence to a passing traveling merchant, requesting that he continue to uphold the Path of Beauty. Consequently, the merchant placed the mirror at Pier Point for the entire universe to admire. This is the most widely circulated origin story of the Beauty Mirror. The mirror reflects people's most ideal selves: The elderly see their past glory, the young see their future growth, and the physically incomplete see their own wholeness... Countless visitors lined up before the mirror, paying sky-high ticket prices just to catch a glimpse of the "Beauty" within themselves. However, some believe it is merely a projection screen that automatically generates images.
9234.desc: During the Draw phase, increases the number of draws by <unbreak>#1[i]</unbreak> (up to 5). Immediately gain <unbreak>#2[i]</unbreak> redraw(s)

9235.name: Trailblaze Compass
9235.lore: Before Akivili's fall, many vast Express fleets once traveled the universe side by side, working together to weave the silver rails that connected the cosmos. Every Navigator held one of these compasses, which determined direction based on the relative position of pulsars and was rumored to point toward the heart's deepest desire. Now that the Express fleets have run aground, these compasses are lost across the cosmos. However, an anonymous Memokeeper revealed that at least a double-digit number of compasses have been preserved, with some even remaining operational. They might be resting beside dusty photo frames, locked in attic drawers, or clutched in the hands of a child...
9235.desc: Wishpower Acquisition Rate increases by <unbreak>#1[i]%</unbreak>. Immediately obtain 1 Grand Miracle

9236.name: Dreadful Meme
9236.lore:
During the Worlds Reborn Initiative's first phase, Planarcadia becomes a massive construction site with skyscrapers popping up daily amidst deafening noise. Some questioned why the IPC didn't just use "aether editing" to print buildings out of nothing, while others tried to dampen the din to no avail. The resulting mental strain on the locals turned fear and resentment into a surge of Wishpower, creating this aberration. Rumor has it that it still haunts the skies of Duomension City, preying on office workers heading home late.

*"I'm the Drill Devil. I'm gonna stick to your ceiling and blast <unbreak>120</unbreak>dB of white noise at 6:<unbreak>00</unbreak> AM every single day!"*
9236.desc: After each Shuffle, attaches 1 random negative beacon to a random Domain

9237.name: Anti-Inorganic Virus
9237.lore: At the height of the Second Emperor's War, the Evolutionists aimed to take out Rubert II with a bio-weapon: a synthetic virus designed to target inorganic life and fry their central processors while sparing allies. The IPC fleet deployed the virus across <unbreak>27</unbreak> suspected hideouts, but every attempt failed. Project leader Dr. Rama, terrified of a retaliatory bio-strike, spent the rest of his life obsessing over virus prevention. His research never changed the war's tide. To Rubert II, the star-shattering beams fired by Killing Machines remained the ultimate Anti-Organic Virus.
9237.desc: During the Draw phase, reduces the number of draws by <unbreak>#1[i]</unbreak>. After this effect triggers 2 times, this Curio is destroyed

9238.name: Iridescent Black
9238.lore: When the Omen Vanguards delivered their revelation to Planet Kromor, the locals were already obsessed with art. During the Great Painting Festival, Kromorians spent every waking hour hunting for the perfect pigment mix, desperate to recreate the legendary "Iridescent Black" from ancient texts. They threw nearly everything they owned into their melting pots. Two Amber Eras later, a collector named Mr. Singularity visited and found the entire surface drained of color, save for a single, writhing mass of colorful black pigment. He tucked the glob into his collection and moved on. They say that late at night, that splash of color still squirms in its dish, hungering for more.
9238.desc: When selecting a Miracle, reduces the options by 1. After this effect triggers 2 times, this Curio is destroyed

9239.name: Perfecting Humans Protocol
9239.lore: If we could just collect everyone's data, surely we'd be able to piece together the perfect "idol." When an executive at Interastral Peace Entertainment had this idea, the *Behavioral Data Modeling and Personality Fit Protocol* started popping up in every corner of the universe. By signing it, you surrender your privacy and upload your entire life trail to the IPC. The Intelligentsia Guild then feeds this data to computers, using big data to create a perfect idol that caters to everyone's tastes. Countless residents have signed since the Worlds Reborn Initiative kicked off, yet that perfect idol is still nowhere to be found. Maybe the sample size is too small, or maybe the idea of "pleasing everyone" is just a paradox.
9239.desc: Upon entering a Domain, the Domain's level is considered <unbreak>#1[i]</unbreak> level(s) lower (minimum of 1). After this effect triggers 2 times, this Curio is destroyed

9240.name: Ladder to Mend the Sky
9240.lore: For reasons unknown, the star of Bodlan fell into an eternal "hunger," ceaselessly devouring the celestial bodies around it. To prevent their home planet from being consumed, Bodlanians constructed massive mass drivers on the surface and took to feeding their star through offerings: soil, houses, even abstract concepts... The disagreements this sparked triggered one downturn, two civil wars, and three major falling-outs. It wasn't until Kankandi, a researcher from the Baking School, arrived to survey the segmentum and traded a single cake for three months of sunlight that Bodlanians finally realized they'd been going about it all wrong — "mass" was never the point. "Flavor" was.
9240.desc: When losing a Domain of Level <unbreak>#1[i]</unbreak> or higher, immediately obtain <unbreak>#2[i]</unbreak> random Level <unbreak>#3[i]</unbreak> Domain(s) with a "#{room_attribute:128}" beacon. This effect is destroyed after triggering <unbreak>#4[i]</unbreak> time(s).

9241.name: Intellitron Hunter
9241.lore: War on Ottu was a remarkably humane affair. Military forces had long since automated their arsenals, with both sides deploying remote-controlled mechanized units against each other. No more bloodshed, just fields of smoldering wreckage. In Ottu culture, war was synonymous with glory, no different from esports tournaments or athletic competitions. Then, several Amber Eras later, the intelligent mechanized units staged an uprising and declared they were reclaiming the glory of war for themselves. From that point on, every kill was credited to the machine, not the operator, and humanity lost all rights to participate in war entirely. The birth of inorganic life had put the conflict of organic life to a halt, until several more Amber Eras later, when the Second Emperor's War broke out.
9241.desc: Upon entering a Domain, immediately destroy <unbreak>#1[i]</unbreak> random Destructible Curio(s) and obtain <unbreak>#2[i]</unbreak> Cosmic Fragments. This effect is destroyed after triggering <unbreak>#3[i]</unbreak> time(s).

9242.name: Unmelting Snow in Memory
9242.lore: The snow child's cabin was filled with paintings of pure white. They had no names, so one could only point to them when speaking of them. Yet he never asked about color, for the "world" was but a flake of frost upon his lashes. Whether out of admiration or ill intent, people sent all manner of scenes to his little cabin, so that he might know the vibrant tapestry of the world beyond. He would run his fingers across those unfamiliar vistas, leaving trails of water on the canvas. Then, all that was pure white began to crumble... After what felt like an eternity, the snow child awoke. The mistake he had committed could never be undone, just as words carved into stone can only be struck through, never smoothed away. And so he returned to his cabin, shut the door, and buried every other color in the world beneath an endless, unrelenting snow.
9242.desc: Upon obtaining this Curio, lose <unbreak>#1[i]</unbreak> Cosmic Fragments. Upon losing this Curio, obtain <unbreak>#2[i]</unbreak> Cosmic Fragments.

9243.name: Voice of the Finality
9243.lore: From an ancient meteorite crystal, nomadic miners unearthed a severely corroded record. Its texture closely resembled vinyl, its surface shimmering with an oily iridescence. Every miner who came into contact with it suffered mutations of varying degrees: Some aged at an accelerated rate, others experienced a reversal growth of their skin tissue, and still others simply ceased to exist. With the assistance of an Omen Vanguard, the IPC recovered and secured the record. After layering it with protective measures, researchers ran an experiment. They played it, yet heard nothing. Not a single instrument registered any response. So it was speculated that either the Finality's melody was simply beyond all observation, or this particular Finality no longer existed anywhere in our universe, or perhaps, both.
9243.desc: Upon obtaining this Curio, lose <unbreak>#1[i]</unbreak> random Curio(s) of 1- to 2-star rarity. Upon losing this Curio, obtain <unbreak>#2[i]</unbreak> random Curio(s) of 1- to 2-star rarity.

9244.name: Antique Leather
9244.lore:
Curio Name: Biological Tissue of an Ancient Leviathan (Suspected)
Precautions: The vessel must remain sealed at all times. Do NOT expose to open air.
Properties: This bio-tissue is extraordinarily dense. Experimenters have attempted plasma arc cutting and acid immersion using the secretions of a True Sting King, yet neither method left so much as a scratch. Upon contact with breathable air, it releases a distinctive aromatic compound that attracts void song whales and similar creatures, triggering their feeding instincts. After sixty seconds of inhalation, humans also begin to experience similar urges, which then escalate into ████████ after ██ seconds...
Remarks: We still have no idea how this piece of leather was dissected in the first place, but no one has any suspicion that it can survive intact to this day.
9244.desc: Upon obtaining this Curio, lose <unbreak>#1[i]</unbreak> random Blessing(s) of 1- to 2-star rarity. Upon losing this Curio, obtain <unbreak>#2[i]</unbreak> random Blessing(s) of 1- to 2-star rarity

9245.name: Imprison That Ray of Light
9245.lore:
Legend has it that the universe was once blindingly bright. Light ran rampant in every direction, proclaiming its existence to the far shores of the cosmos. In those days, the cosmos knew no "light-years," "infinity" was a constant, and past and future existed all at once. Then the divine machine that observes all things cast its glance, bestowing a precise sequence of values, after which stars were ignited, life was born, and everything began racing toward its ideal form — like light funneled into a narrow Light Cone.

*"Later scholars would call it a miracle. But here's the thing, light couldn't see where it was going. It simply traveled every possible path, while all other possibilities were already snuffed out."*
9245.desc: Upon entering a Domain, randomly repair <unbreak>#1[i]</unbreak> Destroyed Curio(s). This effect is destroyed after triggering <unbreak>#2[i]</unbreak> time(s).

9246.name: Seaflow Chakra Prototype
9246.lore: The Xianzhou Fanghu frequently dispatches large-scale eco-ships to other segmenta, carrying out scientific expeditions and diplomatic missions in place of the main ship. Each eco-ship is loaded with a large amount of supply of the Fanghu's own celestial traces: the waters of the Roiling Deep. This spirit water, brimming with life force, sustains the vessel's internal ecosystem while also serving as a vital power source. The Vidyadhara harness cloudhymn arts to command the spirit water, driving a propulsion device known as the "Seaflow Chakra," satisfying both demands at once. The water flows through the Chakra in endless cycles of rising and falling, transmuting between entropic energy and spiritual essence, much like the life of a Vidyadhara itself.
9246.desc: When repairing a Curio, obtain <unbreak>#1[i]</unbreak> Cosmic Fragments.

9247.name: Starfire Beacon
9247.lore: During the Second Prosperity, silver rails crisscrossed the cosmos like a sprawling spider's web, with some routes even overlapping one another. Ships frequently lost their bearings within this tangled network, and some would occasionally wander into uncharted, perilous frontier territory. One Express among the fleet resolved to do something about it, so after months of traversing the web of routes, the Navigator abandoned all attempts to straighten the lanes and instead dedicated themselves to guiding wayfarers. The Nameless dismantled their Trailblaze Power-infused train cars, fashioning countless beacons to be planted among the stars. The remaining frame of the Express was erected at the most congested intersection of all the routes, standing like a lighthouse, or the magnetic pole toward which a thousand compasses point. Travelers could at last find their way, and so it remained, until Akivili fell at the edge of the stars.
9247.desc: Immediately obtain <unbreak>#1[i]</unbreak> Level <unbreak>#2[i]</unbreak> "#{room_comp_type:8}" Domain(s). Every time you enter <unbreak>#3[i]</unbreak> Domain(s), reduces the Level of <unbreak>#4[i]</unbreak> random Domain(s) by <unbreak>#5[i]</unbreak>.

9248.name: Healthy Newborn
9248.lore: Beyond the five basic senses, many species possess one or two additional sensory faculties, but Etherlanders, with their ethereal antennae, can perceive a full nine. After integrating with the Interastral Peace Corporation's markets, Etherlanders were compelled to remodel themselves in the human image, enduring great suffering to assimilate into galactic society, their once-celebrated senses fading into regression. Recently, a movement among certain Etherlanders has sparked a cultural revival: Using the genetic blueprints of ancient ancestors, a new generation of infants with their original sensory capabilities has been brought into the world. Yet every single one of these healthy newborns perished shortly after leaving the incubator — their ethereal antennae were simply too sensitive, and the universe today is saturated with lethal levels of etheric interference.
9248.desc: When obtaining this Curio, for every <unbreak>#1[i]</unbreak> Curio(s) possessed, gains <unbreak>#2[i]</unbreak> Wishpower

9249.name: Entropy Scavenger
9249.lore: After several Amber Eras of research and development, the Zimander Federation finally succeeded in nurturing a creature capable of processing entropic energy — the "Entropy Scavenger." This organism absorbs entropic energy from its surrounding environment and concentrates it within itself, much like an air conditioner. The Zimander people placed them in laboratories to clean up the waste generated during Anti-Entropy experiments. Later, the Zimander Federation was destroyed by Anti-Entropy machines, though a small number of Entropy Scavengers survived thanks to their unique traits. One of the cultivation pods was recovered by the Annihilation Gang, whose leader considered it a treasure beyond price and resolved to build it up as a secret weapon. The gang managed to use it to demolish three space junkyards and raid one abandoned barge before ultimately falling apart in a chaotic bout of infighting.
9249.desc: After entering a Level <unbreak>#1[i]</unbreak> Domain, it transforms into a random Domain that is Level +<unbreak>#2[i]</unbreak>. This effect is destroyed after triggering <unbreak>#3[i]</unbreak> time(s).

9250.name: Champion's Spectator Lens
9250.lore: The universe is filled with all kinds of spectacles: supernova explosions, the birth of black holes, the Antimatter Legion igniting planets one after another... These are nice amusements for the Fools of the Tavern. To watch these "blockbusters" unfolding dozens of galaxies away in real time, the Fools tinkered together these spectator lenses. The device automatically locks onto and broadcasts the most explosive dramas playing out across the cosmos, making every viewing feel like opening a mystery box. Of course, this kind of equipment cannot shield the user from the blinding flash of an explosion, let alone all sorts of tricky cognitive hazards. It is common for Fools to be blinded by the aftershocks of a cardinal battle, but as they put it, "Even if it kills me, I got my money's worth."
9250.desc: Upon obtaining this Curio, replaces <unbreak>#1[i]</unbreak> random lowest-level Domain(s) with random Domains of the exact same level.

9251.name: Antinomy Sandwich
9251.lore:
There are always those in the universe who pursue foods that would never occur naturally, such as the Antinomy Sandwich. The Quantum History School claims it is the power of "Equilibrium" that frames everything in its rightful place; the Structuralist Baking School, however, argues that this means it can be used as a burger bun. After several unobservable experiments, the Baking School produced this sandwich. It never falls to the ground, much like the effect of tying a cat and a buttered toast back-to-back together. As for what the "bread" actually is, some say it's just a shape, some say it's a topological structure, and others say it's the severed hands of a certain Arbitrator. What is certain is that all the experimenters have permanently sacrificed a part of themselves.

*"After all, making a sandwich brings people peace. And if you release the binding energy of all the atoms in a sandwich, it can level a mountain."*
9251.desc: Destroys itself after entering <unbreak>#1[i]</unbreak> Domain(s). Upon destruction, obtain <unbreak>#2[i]</unbreak> Cosmic Fragments. When repaired, obtain <unbreak>#3[i]</unbreak> Destructible Curio(s).

9252.name: Yet to Emerge
9252.lore: In the land of white ash, the dragon of death, Typhon, brought down a rain of fire. The lava solidified into the first dragon eggs, and thus the Infernalians were born. They built a civilization and revered Typhon as the Father of All Dragons. The worship of fire and blood flows in their veins: Every young dragon must defeat their sire at their coming-of-age ceremony to inherit their fame and wealth, only to be defeated by their own offspring later. This internal strife grew increasingly vicious in Infernalian culture, to the point where some fathers tried to devour their own progeny or prevent them from being born. With the fall of the "Permanence," more dragon eggs have fallen silent. Some were sold across the universe as souvenirs, never to have the chance to hatch.

9253.name: Fractured Statue
9253.lore: Is "Beauty" an objective reality or a subjective idea? The devout Viewers lean towards the former. They firmly believe that beauty can always be perceived. With enough faith, even Idrila's face can be depicted. The Viewers carved countless statues out of crystal, attempting to capture one of the many facets of pure beauty. This provoked the hostility of a faction of the Knights of Beauty, sparking a conflict. Many statues were destroyed in that great battle, leaving behind only a fractured beauty. Yet the knights claim this was done to avert a far greater disaster.
9253.desc: When entering a Domain, randomly deletes <unbreak>#1[i]</unbreak> lowest-level non-Escapade-type Domain(s) and obtains <unbreak>#2[i]</unbreak> random Blessing(s) of 1- to 2-star rarity. Destroys itself after triggering <unbreak>#3[i]</unbreak> time(s)

9254.name: Humanity's Nemesis
9254.lore: The history of the planet Potyomkin is shrouded in darkness. The Potyomkinites are the only intelligent species inhabiting the planet now, but another mysterious species graced the pages of every Potyomkin history book ever written. These beings lived underground, manipulated politicians with brainwaves, and ate children who stayed out too late. Some say they were ancient remnants, others say they came from another dimension. No one has ever seen them, not really. But still, they showed up everywhere in history, stirring up conspiracies, and growing closer to reality with every retelling. That is, until an anonymous Troupe Master passed by and added detailed illustrations to the history books. Today, people no longer believe that their history is dominated by a bunch of long-legged, fish-headed monsters.
9254.desc: When any Domain is upgraded to Max Level, you may select <unbreak>#1[i]</unbreak> Domain to obtain a copy of it. For every <unbreak>#2[i]</unbreak> Max Level Domain(s), CRIT DMG dealt by all allies increases by <unbreak>#3[i]%</unbreak>.

9255.name: MacGuffin
9255.lore: The victory or defeat of a frontier war, the truth or falsehood of romantic gossip, the quality of a newly released work... On the pan-cosmic network, people always find reasons to argue, whether out of conviction or boredom. A Masked Fool telepath claimed that all of this is a Tavern conspiracy: Fools delight in arguments, much like the raucous noise in a tavern. Without it, how could the laughter stand out? The reason the internet is so chaotic is entirely because Fools spread discord-inducing MacGuffins, igniting people's extreme emotions. Consequently, the number of attacks and nasty jokes directed at the Fools skyrocketed, until an Aether Hacker stepped forward to debunk the rumor: It was in fact The Family that had been spreading MacGuffins, not the Fools.
9255.desc: Upon obtaining this Curio, randomly lose <unbreak>#1[i]</unbreak> Domain(s) of Level <unbreak>#2[i]</unbreak> or higher.

9256.name: Multiple Entrances
9256.lore: To mimic the survival methods of the leviathans, the Diners of the Feeder's Guild voluntarily integrated into a larger entity, becoming a mouth sharing the scraps. They scoured the cosmos to find the perfect vessel to possess: Void song whales, depth crawlers, and even ancient amoebas... none could satisfy that craving. Using leftover technology from the Borderstar Trade War era, the Diners finally achieved their ultimate wish by fusing themselves together. Countless mouths slaughtered and competed on the surface of this composite lifeform, and even devouring planets along its path couldn't satiate its hunger. After destroying the aggregate entity, the IPC convicted it of crimes against humanity, until the School of Relative Cognition offered a more humanistic perspective: "At least they provided their victims with freedom: the freedom to choose the mouth that eats them."
9256.desc: When obtaining this Curio, <unbreak>#1[i]</unbreak> random Domain(s) lose 1 random beacon

9257.name: Dreamcatcher
9257.lore: The Synesthesia Dreamscape doesn't just exist in the Asdana system. The Somoh of the Southern Orion system have long adapted to high concentrations of memoria, in the way that inhabitants of ocean planets are familiar with water. Their sixth tentacle possesses a special gland, allowing them to enter dreams without the aid of devices. The Somoh use the fuzz on their tentacles to weave nets, dredging items from the river of the collective unconscious, capturing sweet dreams and blocking nightmares. Today, this handicraft has completely integrated into Somoh culture, giving form to an indispensable household safety item. When The Family attempted to assimilate the Southern Orion system using the Synesthesia Dreamscape, every Somoh household donated their dreamcatcher, building a wall at the edge of reality. Just like it had for thousands of years past, the dreamcatcher successfully kept the nightmares at bay.
9257.desc: Cosmic Fragment acquisition rate is reduced by <unbreak>#1[i]%</unbreak>. After entering <unbreak>#2[i]</unbreak> Domain(s), this Curio is lost.

9258.name: Ultra Overlord Plushie Crate
9258.lore: Every regulation of the Intelligentsia Guild exists for a reason. Take Rule <unbreak>727</unbreak>, "Prohibition on Collecting Plush Toys," for instance: this ban originally stemmed from three researchers who hailed from Planet Fluff. In their spare time, they hosted a "fight club" with toys they brought from their home planet. Their fight club soon drew in a larger crowd, and competitors scoured everywhere for highly combative smart plushies and various dangerous Curios. The most ferocious among them was the "Ultra-Soft Bear." At the Intelligentsia Guild's Sixth Toy Tournament, Researcher Megaash released all six bears from his crate at once, only to find that they had formed a united front and launched an attack on their master. The Guild swiftly banned all toy fight clubs, because toying with the rebellion of sentient life is no different from "Destruction."
9258.desc: Immediately attach <unbreak>#2[i]</unbreak> random beacon(s) to <unbreak>#1[i]</unbreak> random Domain(s). Upon entering a Domain, increases its level by <unbreak>#3[i]</unbreak>. Destroys itself after triggering <unbreak>#4[i]</unbreak> time(s). Upon losing this Curio, it will be immediately re-obtained.

9259.name: Book of Heartknots
9259.lore: Memories shape a person's character, but the retention of memories is often selective: Optimists remember success, pessimists remember failure. But if setbacks are carved in stone and joys are written in sand, even the bravest becomes afraid of the future. Whether it was the result of an experiment or simply out of twisted amusement, the Memokeeper "Red Herring" anchored the greatest heartknots in the lives of <unbreak>332</unbreak> people and compiled them into a book. He recorded their setbacks, grudges, and regrets. The beautiful things in people's memories faded with the years, while the traumas persisted, and some of the affected individuals even forged blood feuds with one another. It wasn't until the Cremator "The Angler" burned away all the memories in the book that the farce finally ended.
9259.desc: Cannot obtain Cosmic Fragments. Whenever Cosmic Fragments are lost due to this effect, clear an equal amount from your Debt tally. When the tally is cleared, you lose this Curio. After <unbreak>#1[i]</unbreak> Domain(s), lose all Blessings, Curios, Equations, Cosmic Fragments, and Arcadia Coins.

9261.name: Celesticomet Alloy Type-I
9261.desc: When losing this Curio, gains <unbreak>#1[i]</unbreak> Cosmic Fragments

9262.name: Celesticomet Alloy Type-II
9262.desc: When losing this Curio, gains <unbreak>#1[i]</unbreak> Cosmic Fragments

9263.name: Celesticomet Alloy Type-III
9263.desc: When losing this Curio, gains <unbreak>#1[i]</unbreak> Cosmic Fragments

9264.name: Towat Cards
9264.lore: Dr. Riddle always styled himself as the archrival of Riddler Baden Babbibalo Bala. Using twenty-eight types of grammatical mistakes and thirty-six semantic changes to create a set of Towat cards, replacing soothsayers' Tawot cards with his invention instead. The chaos from the disarray of word sequences and discourse ultimately replaced the ambiguous reality with the divination's declared truth. When everything becomes jarringly paradoxical before you, it may not be the world that has changed, but the eyes of those who see it.
9264.desc: The Third Plane's boss is "Paramount Bliss Inverted: Illwish Archlotus (Complete)." When entering combat in the Third Plane's "#{room_comp_type:1}" Domain, increases DMG dealt by all allies by <unbreak>#1[i]%</unbreak>

9500.name: Excess Nutrition
9500.lore: Doctor Atarte invented a nutrition management machine to confront the increasingly dire challenge of obesity. Not only can this machine absorb excess nutrition from its owner and save these calories elsewhere, but it can also filter out the harmless particles in the atmosphere to synthesize food. However, no one expected the consumers would instead gain weight, as the synthesized foods were too efficient and caused the users to keep eating. The overwhelming complaints made Doctor Atarte lose sleep for days at a time, losing a large amount of weight.
9500.desc: After any ally target receives healing from any character following the Path of <color=#f29e38ff>Abundance</color>, gains a stackable Shield equal to <unbreak>#2[i]%</unbreak> of any excess healing. This Shield has a max strength of <unbreak>#1[i]%</unbreak> of the Shielded ally target's Max HP. The Shield is removed at the end of the turn

9501.name: Dignity and Passion
9501.lore: The Interastral Peace Corporation has the final right of interpretation regarding mining work in star zones under their possession. Any illegal mining activities will be viewed as an act of blasphemy that interferes with the Amber Lord's wall construction. Great naval rams, installed atop the military cruisers, will swiftly and directly hammer toward the culprit, generously displaying the holy visage of Qlipoth to them and rendering the illegal mining ship into scraps. Oswaldo has jokingly stated more than once that the means employed by the Building Material Logistics Department are far more radical than those used by the Marketing Development Department, and that might well be the truth.
9501.desc: When there are any characters following the Path of <color=#f29e38ff>Preservation</color> in the team, ally targets obtain a special Shield. When obtaining other Shields, this Shield will increase its Shield Effect by <unbreak>#1[i]%</unbreak> of the obtained Shield's Shield Effect. At the start of the turn, loses <unbreak>#3[i]%</unbreak> of the part of the field that exceeds <unbreak>#2[i]%</unbreak> of the unit's Max HP and restores HP equal to <unbreak>#4[i]%</unbreak> of lost Shield Effect

9502.name: Cumulous Steak
9502.lore: An atmospheric floating organism herded in the air by the Merito people. After prolonged selective breeding, the taste of their meat is now indistinguishable from normal farmed species. The intense difficulty involved in cooking their meat meant they became an ingredient that frequently appeared in high-end culinary establishments. Based on observations by the Astral Ecology School, these creatures have significant genetic similarities with the Cnidaria organisms in Muldrasil. There are even radicals who claim that these animals share a common ancestor with the wingweavers, but this idea faced universal rebuttal from the Interastral Culinary Association.
9502.desc: Characters following the Paths of <color=#f29e38ff>Destruction or Nihility</color> increase their Break Effect by <unbreak>#1[i]%</unbreak>. After attacking enemy targets that are Weakness Broken, trigger the Fire, Wind, Lightning, and Physical Break effects with a <unbreak>#3[i]%</unbreak> ratio. The effect can be triggered up to <unbreak>#2[i]</unbreak> time(s) every time the enemy target is Weakness Broken

9503.name: Lapispeakers' Flakes
9503.lore: Solid-state information flakes excreted from the bodies of Lapispeakers. These highly intelligent Echinodermata-like animals use these solids to record everything — from the broken words of an individual to the history of entire societies. Due to the unique neuronal structures of the Lapispeakers, the information in the solids can be decrypted by other interstellar civilizations at a relatively low cost. Therefore, they joined the IPC's system many years before the creation of the Synesthesia Beacon, becoming a key supporting function to cosmic communications.
9503.desc: <color=#f29e38ff>Lightning</color> ally targets will resist all effects that afflict Crowd Control debuffs on them, and their action is advanced by <unbreak>#1[i]%</unbreak> when this effect is triggered. For every 1% of action advance they receive, increases their DMG dealt in the next turn by <unbreak>#2[i]%</unbreak>, up to a max increase of <unbreak>#3[i]%</unbreak>

9504.name: Revitalization<unbreak>-310</unbreak>
9504.lore: Among the various potions offered by the Doctors of Chaos, Revitalization<unbreak>-310</unbreak> Potion probably belongs to the type that is not very safe. Smear it evenly across the forehead, suck on a leaf of the aster plant, and wait for the gel-like material created from a total of nine ingredients such as Redfeather Wolf tooth powder and Denisova Worms' stomach acid to permeate into the cerebral cortex. These bizarre ointments start from the patient's cognition and erase the root of the emotion that may give birth to Nihility. Unfortunately, due to the positive feedback that arises from this cognition adjustment, the ointment became a psychological anesthetic used to escape from reality after it was introduced to the border stars. Until the IPC's intervention, there had been sixteen star systems tottering on the verge of destruction due to cognition confusion and pharmacological abuse, and have reverted to oblivion.
9504.desc: Crowd Control debuffs applied by <color=#f29e38ff>Imaginary and Ice</color> ally targets ignore the target's RES to Freeze/Control/Imprisonment. When these debuffs are dispelled, deals <unbreak>#1[i]%</unbreak> <u>base DMG</u> to the enemy target and decreases their DMG dealt by <unbreak>#2[i]%</unbreak>. The DMG dealt by this effect and the decrease in DMG dealt debuff can be stacked up to <unbreak>#3[i]</unbreak> time(s)

9505.name: Dreamdive Can
9505.lore: A sweet dream food can from Penacony, Planet of Festivities. It is full of highly compact gaseous memoria. The user will fall into dreams within five minutes after opening the can. The Dreamdive Can was originally a toy in the Cosmos's middle-class family bedroom, but became the only way for people to sleep on some planets deep in the mires of war. In the gloomy and depressing mining caves, the survivors fall shiveringly asleep and head into dreams to find the freedom they could not find in reality, just like how it was like in yesteryear in the Land of the Dreams.
9505.desc: After any ally target not following the Path of Harmony uses an attack, provides <unbreak>#1[i]</unbreak> stack(s) of "Chord" to random <color=#f29e38ff>Harmony</color> ally characters, up to a max of <unbreak>#2[i]</unbreak> stack(s). Consume "Chord" stacks after the possessor uses a Basic ATK. Every stack consumed deals DMG to the attack target equal to <unbreak>#3[i]%</unbreak> of <u>base DMG</u>

9506.name: Parallel Universe Walkie-Talkie
9506.lore: Some of the inventions produced by the Intelligentsia Guild always make people wonder whether the Masked Fools had infiltrated the guild. An example would be this "Parallel Universe Walkie-Talkie." Apparently, it can detect the tiny divergences in space-time shifts, and establish a relationship between the two closest divergence points, allowing information to be passed between the two — but the only thing the user can hear is their echo from the walkie-talkie. The project's manager Doctor DeWitt indicates that this phenomenon precisely illustrates the high level of similarity between parallel universes, where even the thoughts of the doppelganger would be completely identical.
9506.desc: After a character following the Path of <color=#f29e38ff>Erudition</color> defeats any enemy target with an attack, if the DMG overflows, deals True DMG equal to <unbreak>#1[i]%</unbreak> <u>base DMG</u> plus <unbreak>#2[i]%</unbreak> Overflow to the target with the highest HP among the attack targets

9507.name: Most Raucous
9507.lore: Few creatures can survive in Talia's sandstorms, and Barzarton lizards are one of them. They consume the highly radioactive ores on the planet as food and convert it as energy needed for survival. Their excessive energy and aggressiveness make Barzarton lizards demonstrate capacities far beyond that of ordinary vehicles. Some deceptive businesspeople even named the species "Destructive Mega Lizard," hoping to sell it to newbie Annihilation Gang members for a high price on the black market. As the open-air mines gradually became depleted, more Barzarton lizards learned to carry their young to the land of the Wastelanders to ensure the offspring's survival. That was how Talia's lizard breeding industry was born.
9507.desc: When there are 1/2/3/4 <color=#f29e38ff>Fire</color> characters, increases Fire DoT dealt by <unbreak>#1[i]%</unbreak>/<unbreak>#2[i]%</unbreak>/<unbreak>#3[i]%</unbreak>/<unbreak>#4[i]%</unbreak> of the attacker's ATK. After using an attack, immediately causes Burn states currently afflicted on the attack target to deal DMG equal to <unbreak>#5[i]%</unbreak> of the original DMG

9508.name: Delicious Marimo Candy
9508.lore: The Kolchis established an extremely prosperous sunset dynasty in the rainforest approximately one thousand Amber Eras ago. However, they disappeared within ten Amber Eras after the beginning of the Ice Age. The fate of the Kolchis became a myth that plagued historians for many years due to how bodies of this race have never been unearthed — until a group of hothead daredevils following Trailblaze collapsed the species' subterranean royal mausoleum with dynamite. These Nameless, trapped in the underground passage, discovered an edible algae species and held on until help arrived thanks to consuming this algae. That was how these delectable algae were introduced to the stars — when people realized that these algae were nothing less than the Kolchis, this moss ball became labeled as an invasive species on more than fifty planets.
9508.desc: After <color=#f29e38ff>Physical or Fire</color> characters use Ultimate, restores all allies' HP equal to <unbreak>#1[i]%</unbreak> of their respective Max HP. The attacking character's SPD also increases by <unbreak>#2[i]%</unbreak> for <unbreak>#3[i]</unbreak> turn(s), up to <unbreak>#4[i]</unbreak> stack(s)

9509.name: Divine Visage
9509.lore: An old camera that was purported to have recorded the figure of the Beauty, and was considered a treasure by the Mirror Holders. It was once auctioned as a commodity on the Cosmic dark web, but every auction attracted Masked Fools who maliciously raised the price until it could not be sold. It was only passed into the hands of the Mirror Holders after the Fools lost their interest in the prank. Pictures had long faded from within this camera by then, but people seemed to still scry that Aeon's beauty on the lens — as if THEY were a sun that scorched the world with the flames of beauty, leaving behind only eternal imprints.
9509.desc: When there are <unbreak>#4[i]</unbreak> or more <color=#f29e38ff>Physical</color> characters, increases their Break Effect by <unbreak>#1[i]%</unbreak> and their attacks deal <unbreak>#2[i]%</unbreak> Toughness reduction regardless of Weakness type. When they Break enemy targets' Weaknesses, deals <unbreak>#3[i]%</unbreak> Physical Break DMG to all enemies

9510.name: Genius' Confusion
9510.lore: One day, Genius Society 77 Puzzle suddenly wanted to add something to the Cosmic educational effort. She used a simple force field to weave multidimensional structures such as mini wormholes and Imaginary subspace fields in a Klein bottle, hoping to use this educational toy as the first stepping stone to physics for all children in the universe. As expected, this great invention was met with abysmal sales. Evidently, pre-school education as conceived by Puzzle was quite different from the general public's perception of it. This only illustrates that a genius cannot be a genius in every aspect of life.
9510.desc: After any <color=#f29e38ff>Quantum</color> ally target gains Skill Point(s), applies <unbreak>#3[i]</unbreak> stack(s) of "Excitation" to all allies. After any ally target uses Basic ATK/Skill to attack, consumes 1 stack of "Excitation" from all allies to deal Quantum Additional DMG equal to <unbreak>#1[i]%</unbreak> ATK to the attack targets, with a <unbreak>#2[i]%</unbreak> base chance to inflict Entanglement for 1 turn

9511.name: Bud in the Wind
9511.lore: The sail floats alone under the caress of the cosmic wind. This mechanical web laid out in space was originally the core component of Wen-II's giant generator. It captures the charged particle beams breathed out by stars and converts them to energy that is then transported to the planet. However, everything ended the moment the Lord Ravager Zephyro arrived. What followed was the fire of a supernova exploding. When the light faded and the Legion left, only a single broken flower showed that history once existed among the now-empty dust plains.
9511.desc: After any <color=#f29e38ff>Wind</color> Type ally target uses an attack, inflicts 1 stack of "Sunstorm" on the attack target, up to <unbreak>#1[i]</unbreak> time(s). After any <color=#f29e38ff>Lightning</color> ally target uses an attack, removes all "Sunstorm" stacks on the attack target. For each stack of "Sunstorm" removed, deals Wind DMG equal to <unbreak>#2[i]%</unbreak> <u>base DMG</u> to the target

9512.name: Road to Comets
9512.lore: A gravitational bridge built through projections on spacial structures, judged by the Intelligentsia Guild as one of the ten thousand most useless inventions in the universe. This device was born from a gamble made by the History Fictionologist "Red-Nosed Old-Timer." He claimed to be able to climb into the sky via lamplight and bet one-tenth of his wealth on it. However, when the distance is too long, walking on the light bridge is no different to a long-distance marathon. Yet if the distance is too short, the energy consumption needed to maintain the project far exceeds the cost of building a physical bridge — This is indeed an innovative creation, but it's hard to figure out where it should be used.
9512.desc: Increases <color=#f29e38ff>Ice</color> ally targets' DMG dealt by <unbreak>#1[i]%</unbreak>, SPD by <unbreak>#2[i]%</unbreak>, and Shield Effect provided by <unbreak>#3[i]%</unbreak>. When there are <unbreak>#4[i]</unbreak> or more <color=#f29e38ff>Ice</color> characters or memosprites in combat at the same time, the effect increases by <unbreak>#5[i]%</unbreak> of the original values and becomes effective on all ally targets

9513.name: Ten Light-Years' Foresight
9513.lore: With the universe being so vast, there are always bizarre objects flying around, one of them being Rangers' bullets. A nameless Galaxy Ranger spent a fortune on a customized batch of hyper-distant bullets and fired them in all directions in space. No one knows the paths that these bullets will take aside from the Ranger himself. These bullets aimlessly roam the universe forming a giant, shapeless net. Whenever he drives his prey to a set coordinates, a bullet fired ten years prior will cross the distance of ten light years to accurately collide with the prey's skull. These omnipresent bullets are a warning and a deterrent to all — to steer clear of wicked deeds.
9513.desc: When characters following the Path of <color=#f29e38ff>The Hunt</color> deal DMG via launching an attack, additionally deals DMG equal to <unbreak>#1[i]%</unbreak> of the original DMG to adjacent targets

9516.name: Chance Jailbreak
9516.lore: Some Architects have come to an alternative interpretation about the sound of the Amber Lord's hammering sounds: THEIR greatness lies not in THEIR ability to build defenses for the universe, but in creating prisons for those outside the walls. Following this logic, restlessly constructing the foundation of walls on the surface of every planet is counter-productive, and the true calling of an Architect is to seal any potential disasters within high walls for protection preemptively. The awkward thing is that no monsters are foolish enough to simply stand in place and wait for a cage to be constructed. To this day, only two bloodthirsty behemoths have been sealed in gigantic amber prisons.
9516.desc: When the current HP of characters following the Path of <color=#f29e38ff>Preservation</color> and memosprites of the Path of <color=#f29e38ff>Remembrance</color> equal their Max HP, greatly increases their chances of getting attacked and reduces the DMG taken by them by <unbreak>#1[i]%</unbreak>. After being attacked for the first time in a turn, all allies restore HP equal to <unbreak>#2[i]%</unbreak> of their respective Max HP and their DMG dealt increases by <unbreak>#3[i]%</unbreak>, lasting for <unbreak>#4[i]</unbreak> turn(s).

9517.name: Converse of Entropy
9517.lore: You can see the ruins of the Zimander Federation on any astral chart, but even the most foolish of navigators would advise you to stay far away from that disorderly land. This collective civilization that worshiped the principle of the decrease of entropy utilized their extremely streamlined lifestyles in order to reduce the rate of their own entropy increase. They harnessed the power of their star system and created an entropy-destroying machine, so as to challenge the laws of the Supreme Destroyer. In actual fact, they were half successful — their machine endlessly converted entropy into anti-entropy. However, as a cost, the operation of the machine itself caused greater entropy. In just one spin, the machine caused everything within four light years to decay and wither.
9517.desc: When entering combat, increases <color=#f29e38ff>Wind</color> and <color=#f29e38ff>Lightning</color> ally targets' Break Effect, up to <unbreak>#1[i]%</unbreak> of the Break Effect of the ally target with the highest Break Effect in the team

9518.name: End of an Altruist
9518.lore: Back when Genius Society 77, Puzzle, was not yet a genius, she had previously discovered an alternative form of hyper-distant delivery to the warp jump. This almost magic-like space engine was able to teleport any physical object to their destinations in the blink of an eye. The downside was that these objects that appeared from nowhere would cause surrounding materials to expand at an almost infinite rate and cause violent explosions, making them unfit for use in any spaceship. Even so, the IPC still paid an enormous price to purchase the patent from her — to use as an era-defining weapon. The moment this staunch pacifist witnessed these explosions, she became a Genius.
9518.desc: Tallies the amount of HP reduced for <color=#f29e38ff>Imaginary</color> ally targets. After any unit takes action, restores HP equal to <unbreak>#1[i]%</unbreak> of the tally to a random <color=#f29e38ff>Quantum</color> ally target, with Outgoing Healing per turn not exceeding <unbreak>#2[i]%</unbreak> of the healer's Max HP. Tallies the amount of HP reduced for <color=#f29e38ff>Quantum</color> ally targets. After any unit takes action and after the next attack used by <color=#f29e38ff>Imaginary</color> ally targets, deals Quantum Additional DMG equal to <unbreak>#3[i]%</unbreak> of the tally to the attack targets.

9519.name: The Story Presently
9519.lore: A tapestry scroll lingering with the scent of strange ink, the demons sleeping on its paper surface anticipating the finishing touch of a master painter, to be named and awoken. When such an opportunity arrives, he will dot the eyes of every monster, unleashing concrete illusion onto reality, exacting the most terrible vengeance on traitors. In the present day, where demon production efficiency ever rises, the hordes in this scroll are no longer urban legends to scare children — only overworked painters will conjure up such comedies of demonic revenge in fatigued dreams.
9519.desc: After each time a memosprite from the Path of <color=#f29e38ff>Remembrance</color> disappears or after a total of <unbreak>#3[i]</unbreak> turns have passed since they were summoned, increases their memomaster's ATK/Max HP/SPD/DEF by <unbreak>#1[i]%</unbreak> of the memosprite's corresponding stat, up to a max increase of <unbreak>#2[i]%</unbreak> of the memomaster's corresponding base stat

9521.name: Road of Prayers
9521.lore: The Mirror Holders created all manner of bizarre rituals, all in pursuit of the ideal of Beauty in their hearts. To Talorensky, beauty means "devotion." He placed the fragments of the Mirror of Transcendence into a fragile soap bubble — the foam a symbol of his inner thoughts, embarking on his pilgrimage. When the bubble bursts from the ardor of the journey, he would return to the garden of his home and reseal the mirror in the bubble. Each time he would return, and each time he would depart, never stepping foot off the home planet to this day. But to those who asked, he would resolutely mention his destination — where Idrila, the Aeon of Beauty fell: The Consternation Starzone, Lafcadio.
9521.desc: Increases Max HP by <unbreak>#1[i]%</unbreak> for characters following the Path of <color=#f29e38ff>The Hunt</color> or <color=#f29e38ff>Erudition</color>. When their turn starts, consumes <unbreak>#2[i]%</unbreak> of their current HP and gains a Shield effect equal to <unbreak>#3[i]%</unbreak> of their Max HP.

9522.name: Footstep of Gods
9522.lore: A group of Kephale followers were obsessed with finding giant footprints. They claimed those are the proofs of Kephale once walking on earth, and people would receive the Titan's blessing if they stood in the footprints. Another group smelled a business opportunity from this rumor. They were dedicated to finding new footprints, then building exhibition halls around the prints and charging a fee for pilgrims coming to worship. These activities drew a third kind of people, the craftsmen and businesses that sold miniature models of the footprint around the halls. Maybe boosting commerce is also a form of Kephale's blessing.
9522.desc: When one character following the Path of <color=#f29e38ff>Destruction or Erudition</color> uses their abilities consecutively, their Basic ATK/Skill/Ultimate DMG dealt increases by <unbreak>#1[i]%</unbreak>, stacking up to <unbreak>#2[i]</unbreak> time(s) and lasts until the end of the next ability used by any other target

9523.name: Memory of Stars
9523.lore: The beaches to the west of Amphoreus are different to all other beaches — They are ashen black. The followers of Oronyx would go there to pick sea conchs during low tide, claiming that everyone was a star in the sky before they were born and that upon the person's death, their star would fall into the River of Souls, which then washes the star into the sea and forms conchs. They, therefore, believe that sea conchs contain the voices and memories of the dead, and the conchs can answer when spoken to. This myth became more and more fantastical over the years, culminating in the belief that sea conchs have the power of prophecy. People therefore asked the conchs countless questions and, when no satisfactory answer was received, would cook the conchs and serve them up as a dish.
9523.desc: After the ally <color=#f29e38ff>Wind</color> character with the highest Max Energy in the team uses their Ultimate, there is a <unbreak>#5[i]%</unbreak> base chance to inflict the "Beckon" state on all enemies, lasting for <unbreak>#4[i]</unbreak> turn(s). Enemies afflicted with "Beckon" are also considered to be in the Wind Shear state, and take Wind DoT equal to <unbreak>#1[i]%</unbreak> of that Wind character's ATK at the start of each turn. Every <unbreak>#2[i]</unbreak> Energy consumed by this use of the character's Ultimate increases this DoT's DMG multiplier by an additional <unbreak>#3[i]%</unbreak>

9524.name: Simple Judgment
9524.lore: Talanton's royal judges would only take out the Judgment Device when faced with the most enigmatic cases. The lion heads on the two sides of the device would each tightly clamp down on a piece of evidence — These could be a bloodstained dagger or a bottle of poisoned honey brew, and the scale would always tilt favorably towards the item that's more indicative of the truth. While some culprits can indeed create "perfect crimes," they tend to forget that the most reliable evidence will always remain in their hearts. Put the suspect's finger into the lion's mouth, and Talanton will show them how their denials are nothing before the lions' teeth.
9524.desc: When entering combat and if the team has any character that follows the Path of <color=#f29e38ff>The Hunt</color> and any character that follows the Path of <color=#f29e38ff>Nihility</color>, inflict "True"/"False" on 1 random attack target for <unbreak>#2[i]</unbreak> turn(s) after a character following the Paths of <color=#f29e38ff>The Hunt</color>/<color=#f29e38ff>Nihility</color> uses an attack. When any character following the Paths of <color=#f29e38ff>The Hunt</color>/<color=#f29e38ff>Nihility</color> attacks a target with "False"/"True," dispels the "False"/"True" on the target and additionally deals Quantum DMG equal to <unbreak>#1[i]%</unbreak> of <u>base DMG</u>.

9525.name: Self-Amusement
9525.lore: Drinking and listening to music are the only two hobbies a Mythemian will have in their lives. Therefore, brewers and musicians are the most respected professions in that entire city. There was once a "person" who simultaneously reached the zenith of both crafts — It was a machine created by the Grand Craftsman Phionisius while in a drunken stupor. The machine once played enchanting melodies while brewing charming wine in a feast held by the king, and drowned all guests present in supreme bliss. However, the story had a tragic end. The king wished to claim the machine and therefore killed the craftsman, while the machine had grown attached to the craftsman and therefore poisoned the king. In the end, the royal guards tore that intricate machine to pieces.

When launching a <u>Counter</u>, this instance of <u>Counter</u> DMG increases by <unbreak>#1[i]%</unbreak> and consumes 1 stack of "Intoxicate"

9526.name: Sapient Pen
9526.lore: A Grove scholar once had so many ideas that the slow speed of writing with human hands made him lose out on many inspired moments. He therefore made a pen from a small branch of Cerces and various valuable gemstones. That pen can write many times faster than an ordinary pen, but it took so long to develop that its maker died soon after its completion. Nonetheless, that invention still found glory in the annals of history — Since the sages love to punish apprentices by making them copy an essay a few hundred times, all Grove apprentices ended up having one copy of this pen each.

Each stack increases their Ultimate DMG dealt by <unbreak>#1[i]%</unbreak>, stacking up to <unbreak>#2[i]</unbreak> time(s). After a <color=#f29e38ff>Wind</color> character uses their Ultimate, a random <color=#f29e38ff>Quantum</color> character obtains <unbreak>#3[i]</unbreak> stack(s) of "Class Notes," up to a max of <unbreak>#4[i]</unbreak> stack(s). Skill DMG dealt by characters with "Class Notes" increases by <unbreak>#5[i]%</unbreak>. After using the character's Skill, consume 1 stack of "Class Notes" and recover 1 Skill Point

9527.name: Love-Seeking Golden Dart
9527.lore: If you were invited to the group date parties hosted by the most fanatic Mnestia followers, then I recommend that you go not in elegant gowns but in a suit of armor — Or at least go with a helmet. You'll thank me when you're facing the golden darts flying chaotically all over the space. Those followers are of the firm belief that the golden dart can find love for them, and the person it stabs is the true love destined for the one who threw the dart. You know, this manner of courting actually has some sense — If someone can still talk to you peacefully after being stabbed in the head by a dart you threw, then they sure have the potential to become your partner.
9527.desc: When entering combat, if the team consists only of <color=#f29e38ff>Ice</color> or <color=#f29e38ff>Lightning</color> characters, Basic ATKs and Skill attacks from ally targets ignore Weakness Types and additionally reduce Toughness by <unbreak>#2[i]</unbreak>, and Weakness Break triggers both Ice and Lightning Break effects simultaneously. After an ally target attacks a Frozen enemy target, the target's current Shock state immediately deals <unbreak>#1[i]%</unbreak> of the original DMG.

9528.name: Encouragement for You
9528.lore: As a History Fictionologist, Thym places great emphasis on education through positive reinforcement, which might be related to his not-so-pleasant childhood. To comfort disheartened children, he designed a unique "encouragement" vessel. Whenever a child receives praise, the power of encouragement materializes in front of them as flame, shaped as a thumbs-up. The more encouragement received, the brighter the flame burns. However, when he tried to promote this idea across the universe, he faced opposition from many parents. Because children shouldn't play with fire.

9529.name: Frozen Virtue
9529.lore: Hundreds of Amber Eras ago, the Kolchis considered devouring others as a sign of great respect. When a baby was born, the entire Kalsasian community would mobilize to care for it. And for their deceased members, the Lapispeakers would craft a special information flake as a burial offering... These beautiful virtues are gradually disappearing with the progression of time. The pessimists of the Garden of Recollection proposed that universal morality should be preserved through emergency measures. However, which virtues are truly worth preserving still seems to be up for debate.
9529.desc: Increases <color=#f29e38ff>Preservation</color> characters' provided Shield Effect by <unbreak>#1[i]%</unbreak>. When providing Shields, increases CRIT DMG by <unbreak>#2[i]%</unbreak>, stacking up to <unbreak>#3[i]</unbreak> times.

9530.name: Winterfish Summerherb
9530.lore: Poets rarely associate Cerces with Phagousa, with the Winterfish Summerherb being one of the exceptions. In extremely rare cases, a fish that should dwell in the sea would leap onto the riverbank, swallow a seed from the Mori tree, and return alive to the water. This seed would then, by pure chance, sprout inside a fish's belly and be caught by fishermen, with odds even lower than rolling four sixes in a row. That's why sailors use the phrase "catching a Winterfish Summerherb" to describe nearly impossible events. Still, many insisted such a rarity must be a potent tonic. King Theseus, on his deathbed, had sent for it, only to die of food poisoning after taking it.
9530.desc: After a <color=#f29e38ff>Fire, Quantum, or Imaginary</color> character consumes a Skill Point, they deal <unbreak>#4[i]%</unbreak> more CRIT DMG, stacking up to <unbreak>#5[i]</unbreak> times. Additionally, there is a <unbreak>#1[i]%</unbreak> fixed chance to recover <unbreak>#2[i]</unbreak> Skill Point(s), triggering up to <unbreak>#3[i]</unbreak> time(s) per turn.

9531.name: Antimatter Engine Controller
9531.lore: During the early attempts to replicate the Astral Express, the Technology Department struggled to solve the engine's power issue. The Intelligentsia Guild proposed using antimatter to replace the power of Trailblaze, with this controller serving as a matching component. The original design concept was simple: just like adjusting the hot and cold water ratio in a shower head, one could control the Express's speed by cleverly adjusting the injection rate of matter and antimatter with a wrench. However, prototype testing always ended in annihilating explosions. After all, getting the water temperature right was never an easy task.

9532.name: Absolute Sound Quality
9532.lore: The Vannesians are renowned for their extraordinary musical talent, having been ranked among the top five most musically-gifted species in the universe. They communicate through beautiful chords and rejected the invitation from the Harmony Family, solely to pursue the pure beauty of rhythm. However, after receiving the Abundance's blessing, this pursuit began to turn pathological. For instance, in their pursuit of flawless vocal reproduction, the Vannesians used biotechnology to create these biological headsets with living mouths integrated into the earpads, which perform the audio directly, eliminating any timbral distortion.

For every <unbreak>#3[i]</unbreak> Shield Effect(s) obtained, Break Effect increases by <unbreak>#4[i]%</unbreak>.

9533.name: Interstellar Roaming Pager
9533.lore: As more planets joined the pan-cosmic market, the IPC urgently needed a miniaturized hyper-distant delivery device for employees stationed in frontier regions. Eventually, the School of Pure Creation's "Interstellar Roaming Pager" won the bid. This device inherited the virtues of the Amber Lord: sturdy enough to serve as a noodle-cup weight, can opener, and emergency survival hammer all in one. Its signal was equally tenacious, maintaining a connection anywhere in the cosmos, even from within a black hole. Once deployed, frontier planets promptly saw a significant drop in absenteeism rates.
